structure: Part 4, the notification list (dashboard), read on main in full: the dashboard feature's page.js (id dashboard, slug '', maturity exploring), controller.js (four routes: GET /live-animals the list, POST /live-animals/notifications/{id}/amend, POST /live-animals/notifications to start one, GET /live-animals/start the INS entry; renderDashboard builds the view from page, sort and referenceNumber query parameters), template.njk (amend-refused banner, caption, h1, body, start button form, 'Your notifications' h2, a one-third filter aside with a single reference search form, a two-thirds column with a results count and sort form, one GOV.UK summary card per notification with its actions and eight labelled values, the empty text, and Previous/Next pagination), notification-helper.js (sort options and default, date formatting, commodity label, page clamping, list query string, pagination links, results range and label), copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (61 lines each, same keys; Welsh read for parity), view-model/sort-options.js (localised sort wording by position), view-model/row/index.js (backend row to card), view-model/row/actions.js (per-status actions), flow/notification-action-slugs.js (amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete slugs) and dashboard.fit.spec.js (17 tests across empty state and start, rows and actions, reference search, pagination, the alpha banner, accessibility and the amend-refused banner). To confirm claims I also read shared/paging.js and the status map in shared/kit.js and shared/copy.en.js, which other parts own. Every earlier claim in my keeps still matches the code and is kept; the earlier status-words claim was not in my keeps, so its fact is claimed afresh from this slice. The pages the row actions lead to (view, overview, delete, cancel amend, copy) are out of this slice.

claims.statement: A page number past the last page shows the last page instead.
claims.quote: export const normalizePageNumber = ( page, totalPages = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ) => { if (!Number.isInteger(page) || page < 1 || totalPages <= 0) { return 1 } return Math.min(page, totalPages) }; const currentPage = normalizePageNumber(listed.page, listed.totalPages)
claims.note: mechanism: clamps the page number the backend reports before the page renders it; with no pages at all it shows page one.

claims.statement: The list offers every link out of it with the current page, sort and search in the query string, so a trader coming back lands on the list as they left it.
claims.quote: listQuerySuffix: buildHomeListQueryString({ page: currentPage, sort, referenceNumber })
claims.note: mechanism: the controller publishes the list's own query string to the view; the dashboard template does not use it, so it serves the shared chrome and the pages a card's actions lead to.

claims.statement: A notification submitted without an ITAHC still shows as Submitted with all four submitted actions.
claims.quote: test('a notification submitted without an ITAHC shows Submitted and the four submitted actions' ... await expectSubmittedRowActions(page, reference)

claims.statement: The list never scrolls sideways, either at the default width or at the 769-pixel desktop breakpoint.
claims.quote: const DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT_WIDTH = 769; test('dashboard does not overflow horizontally at desktop' ... await expectDashboardNotToOverflow(page) await page.setViewportSize({ width: DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT_WIDTH, height: 900 }) await expectDashboardNotToOverflow(page)

claims.statement: The list has no serious or critical accessibility violations when empty, when it holds a notification card, and when it shows the could-not-amend banner.
claims.quote: test('empty dashboard has no serious or critical axe violations' ... test('dashboard with a notification card has no serious or critical axe violations' ... await expectNoSeriousOrCriticalViolations(page, 'Dashboard with notification cards')

claims.statement: The list carries an Alpha phase banner saying "This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.", whose "give your feedback by email" link opens an email to the APHA service desk, and the same banner follows the trader onto an answering page.
claims.quote: const FEEDBACK_MAILTO = 'mailto:APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk'; const TAG = 'Alpha' const BODY = 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.' const FEEDBACK_LINK_TEXT = 'give your feedback by email'
claims.note: The banner belongs to the shared chrome, which is another part's; the dashboard fit spec is what proves it on this page.

claims.statement: Pressing the start button on the list takes the trader straight to the "Origin of the import" page.
claims.quote: test('starts a new notification at the origin page' ... await page.getByRole('button', { name: copy.startButton }).click() await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Origin of the import' })).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: Every word the list shows in English has a Welsh counterpart, and the page picks the locale's wording.
claims.quote: title: 'Gwasanaeth hysbysu mewnforio', ... startButton: 'Dechrau hysbysiad newydd', notificationsHeading: 'Eich hysbysiadau', ... emptyText: 'Nid ydych wedi dechrau unrhyw hysbysiadau yn y sesiwn hon.'; const copy = copyFor({ en, cy })
claims.note: Read for key parity rather than string by string: the Welsh file holds the same 61 lines and the same keys as the English one, including the two wording functions actionHidden and the pagination results.

claims.statement: The sort options' visible wording is matched to the four sort values by position rather than by name, so the English wording held beside the values is replaced by the locale's wording in the same order.
claims.quote: const sortOptionText = [ copy.sort.options.arrivalNewest, copy.sort.options.arrivalOldest, copy.sort.options.createdNewest, copy.sort.options.createdOldest ] export const sortOptions = NOTIFICATION_SORT_OPTIONS.map((option, index) => ({ ...option, text: sortOptionText[index] }))
claims.note: mechanism: pairs the sort values with their localised wording. The English wording is held twice, once beside the values in notification-helper.js and once in the copy file.

claims.statement: A card's status tag shows the same word and colour as the notification's status strip, and the list proves it reads "Draft" for a draft, "Submitted" for a submitted notification and "Amend" for one being amended.
claims.quote: status: journeyStrip(journey).status; await expect(page.getByText('Submitted', { exact: true })).toBeVisible(); await expect(page.getByText('Draft', { exact: true })).toBeVisible(); await expect(page.locator('.govuk-tag', { hasText: 'Amend' })).toHaveText('Amend')
claims.note: The words and colours (Draft blue, Submitted green, Amend yellow, Deleted grey) live in the shared kit's status map, which another part owns; a Deleted card never shows because the list drops deleted rows.

claims.statement: The browser tab title of the list page is "Import notification service", the same words as its heading.
claims.quote: pageTitle: copy.title; title: 'Import notification service'
claims.note: Inferred because the shared layout, another part's, turns pageTitle into the document title.

claims.statement: The dashboard helpers hold a way to read a notification's arrival date from its transport answers or its top-level arrival date, but nothing on the list uses it.
claims.quote: export const getArrivalDateIso = (notification) => notification.transport?.arrivalDate ?? notification.arrivalDate ?? null
claims.note: mechanism: reads the arrival date from a notification. A search of src finds no caller outside this file; the card reads journey.arrivalDate directly.

claims.statement: "Copy as new" posts to /live-animals/notifications/<id>/copy.
claims.quote: postAction: pagePath(journey.journeyId, notificationActionSlugs.copy); copy: 'copy'
claims.note: The copy handler and the page it leads to belong to the notification-actions part.
